smell: You asked for "discount codes at checkout". The agent went straight to code and quietly decided that codes stack and never expire.
why: /clarify stops before code and turns silent assumptions into at most 5 questions, each with a proposed default. Stacking and expiry are product decisions, not something the agent should guess.

smell: The agent replies "All tests pass" with a checkmark, but there is no command, no exit code, and no output anywhere in the chat.
why: /verify runs the real checks and reports the command, exit code, and observed result. It ends with VERIFIED or NOT VERIFIED, so a claim without evidence cannot pass.

smell: The diff calls formatCurrency() and reads config.paymentDays. The repo actually has formatMoney() in src/lib/money.js and a dueDays key.
why: /ground maps every helper and config key the change needs to what exists in the repo, with file:line evidence, and flags anything invented.

smell: For a ten-line settings loader, the agent added two new packages to package.json, and one import name does not exist on npm.
why: /deps-check verifies each import and package against the manifest, the standard library, and official docs, and never installs anything. Hallucinated or unnecessary packages show up before they ship.

smell: A bug report says "1,299.00" parses wrong. The fix adds if (input === '1,299.00') return 1299 and the report goes green.
why: /root-cause reproduces the bug, tests a few hypotheses, and rejects special-casing the reported input. The real cause (thousands separators) also breaks 2,500.00.

smell: The change works, but it leaves console.log calls, a try/catch that swallows errors, and a copy of a helper that already exists.
why: /deslop reviews a change for named slop patterns (debug output, swallowed errors, duplicate helpers, fake tests) and reports findings with file:line, so you fix the right things.

smell: You are eighty turns into a chat full of dead ends, and you need to continue tomorrow in a clean session.
why: /handoff writes HANDOFF.md with goal, state, decisions, evidence, open questions, and next steps. A fresh chat can then resume without inheriting the noise. Follow it with /clear.

smell: Asked to fix one quantity bug, the agent proposes renaming a public function and refactoring three unrelated files.
why: /scope writes SCOPE.md before any edit: allowed files, forbidden paths, frozen public API, and a done-when check. Anything outside it is out of bounds.

smell: Tool calls run without asking you, including a terminal command that deletes a folder.
why: /disableAutoApprove (alias /disableYolo) brings back the approval prompt, so a human checks each tool call again. /autoApprove does the opposite.

smell: You added a prompt file, but it does not appear when you type /, and you cannot tell why.
why: /troubleshoot reads the chat debug logs to explain why a customization did not load. /prompts lists and manages prompt files, but it does not diagnose the failure.

smell: Every test feeds valid input and checks the right answer. Nothing tests malformed input, wrong types, or boundary values.
why: /fail-paths enumerates edge cases and failure modes, writes tests for them, and runs them without weakening assertions. Plain /tests often stops at the happy path.

smell: In every new chat you re-explain that this repo uses node:test, ESM, and no new dependencies.
why: /create-instructions turns repeated rules into an instructions file the agent loads automatically, so you stop pasting them. /init can bootstrap one from the codebase.

smell: You are about to commit a diff that touches six files. You have not reread it, and the tests last ran an hour ago.
why: /pre-commit is the final gate. It checks scope, debug output, secrets, stubs, skipped tests, and a fresh test run, then ends with READY or NOT READY.

smell: You want to try a risky alternative design, but you do not want to lose the current conversation and its decisions.
why: /fork copies the conversation into a new session. You can experiment there while the original thread stays intact.
